definitions.gloss: mon — a unit of currency in pre-modern Japan
definitions.explanation: A common small unit of currency in Japan from the medieval period through the Edo period, used until the yen replaced it in 1871. A single mon was a trivial sum, so the word often appears in proverbs and set phrases meaning "a tiny amount of money."

examples.japanese: {一文|いちもん}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{持|も}っていない→持つ：00478_motsu⟧。
examples.english: I don't have a single mon. (= I'm penniless.)

examples.japanese: ⟦そんな→そんな：01645_sonna⟧⟦{物|もの}→物：02259_mono⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{三文|さんもん}→三文：28481_sanmon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{価値|かち}→価値：00131_kachi⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧。
examples.english: Something like that isn't worth even three mon. (= It's worthless.)

examples.japanese: ⟦{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{物価|ぶっか}→物価：03607_bukka⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{文|もん}⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{単位|たんい}→単位：03412_tani⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{表|あらわ}された→表す：01868_arawasu⟧。
examples.english: Prices in the Edo period were expressed in a unit called the mon.

notes:
An old currency unit, replaced by the ⟦{円|えん}→円：00774_en⟧ (yen) in 1871. It survives mainly in idioms that express "a tiny sum."

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {一文|いちもん}{無|な}し: penniless, without a single coin
- ⟦{二束三文|にそくさんもん}→二束三文：06020_nisokusanmon⟧: dirt cheap (lit. two bundles for three mon)
- ⟦{早起|はやお}きは{三文|さんもん}の{徳|とく}→早起きは三文の徳：06335_hayaokihasanmonnotoku⟧: the early bird gets the worm (lit. early rising is worth three mon)

USAGE:
Read ぶん, the same kanji means "sentence; writing"—a separate word. As もん it was also a historical unit for shoe size.
